ov: About 94 species of lizards with long necks, powerful tails and claws and strong legs, from 20 cm long to the 3 m Komodo dragon. Most are carnivores. They have the highest resting metabolism of any living reptile and hunt by active pursuit, like mammals of a similar size.

why.p: Monitors are a staple of the reptile pet trade; the savannah monitor and Ackie dwarf monitor are the most commonly kept.
why.et: Some peoples in India, Nepal, the Philippines, Australia and Africa eat their meat, and in Vietnam and Thailand it is a delicacy.
why.dg: Bites from monitors cause rapid swelling, bleeding problems and shooting pain, likely from mild venom.

rg: Africa, Asia and Oceania, including New Guinea and Australia; the Nile monitor is invasive in South Florida.
df: Mostly smaller reptiles, fish, birds, insects, small mammals and eggs; a few species also eat fruit.
fx: Rock monitors fed different numbers of snails could tell apart numbers up to six.
Nile monitors team up: one lures a crocodile away from her nest while the other digs up the eggs.
notes: RESOLVED (owner approved all suggestions, including the optional ones, 2026-09-29): The fact is confirmed: some monitors can count, and they have "the highest standard metabolic rates of all extant reptiles" with "active-pursuit hunting techniques".
